chicago-marathon-2021.headline: My first World Marathon Major.
memory: The year before Chicago, I ran the virtual marathon in 2020, and I remember how hard it was. By the time I finally got to run Chicago in person in 2021, a lot had changed. I had moved to Denver, and I did the peak of my training at altitude.
My sister was still living in Chicago, so I stayed with her for the weekend. Ryan rode his bike around the city during the race and found different spots along the course to cheer me on.

Chicago was my first World Marathon Major, and that is the biggest thing I remember about the day. Breaking four hours was my goal, and I was very proud to do it, but what mattered even more was finally being part of a major marathon and experiencing the scale and energy of Chicago.

I especially remember finishing in Grant Park. I already had a lot of memories there, and it is such a beautiful spot on Lake Michigan. After I finished, I walked around the park, got a beer, and just soaked in the experience.

photos.alt: Alex Ford running the 2021 Chicago Marathon through Pilsen near West 18th Street and Loomis Street.
photos.caption: Ryan caught me running through Pilsen near 18th and Loomis. He biked around Chicago during the race so he could cheer me on at several different points.

colfax-half-2021.headline: Running my new home with Leah.

milestone.label: Together
milestone.note: We ran the entire half together

memory: The Colfax Half had been canceled in 2020, so getting to run it in 2021 felt great. By then Denver was my new home, and I got to run the whole race with my best friend Leah.
One of the things I remember most is that the half marathon course runs through the Denver Zoo. It is such a distinctive part of the race and made the day feel very connected to the city.
Leah and I stayed together for the entire race and finished in City Park. Afterward, we walked to Leah's home for brunch. It was a great way to finish the morning.

staunton-rocks-half-2022.headline: A beautiful trail day with Frankie.

milestone.label: Together
milestone.note: We ran the entire trail half together

memory: Frankie and I ran the entire Staunton Rocks Half Marathon together. It was a beautiful day in Staunton State Park, and being out on the trail together is what I remember most.
At one point on a downhill, I caught a root and went straight into a somersault. Somehow I popped right back up and kept running. It is still one of the funniest things I remember from the race.
We stayed together all the way through the finish. For me, the memory of Staunton is really the beautiful day and getting to run the whole race with Frankie.

photos.alt: Frankie and Alex running together on the Staunton Rocks Half Marathon trail.
photos.caption: Frankie and I ran the entire Staunton Rocks Half together on a beautiful day in Staunton State Park.

colderbolder-2022.headline: A really cool event with great energy.

milestone.label: What stood out
milestone.note: A day to enjoy, not chase a time

memory: I thought the COLDERBolder was a really cool event. The format stood out to me because there were a bunch of different races based on runners' finish times from a previous BOLDERBoulder or COLDERBolder. It gave the morning a different feel from a normal 5K.
I also remember thinking the Fieldhouse at CU Boulder was a very cool spot for the event. The whole atmosphere felt energetic and positive.
I was there by myself and was not chasing a particular time. I was really just there to enjoy the event, and that is what I remember most about it.

bolderboulder-2022.headline: The 10K that felt like a marathon.
memory: I ran my first BOLDERBoulder by myself in 2022, and what struck me immediately was the energy. It felt like the entire city had turned out for a marathon, even though we were running a 10K.

The course had all kinds of things happening along the way: slip and slides, donut stands, beer stands, people in costumes, and just a constant stream of people making the race feel like a celebration.

The finish at Folsom Field was especially memorable. You come into the CU football stadium and get a lap around the field, and afterward I watched the professional races finish there. That whole experience felt special enough that I came back and ran BOLDERBoulder again the next year.

bolderboulder-2023.headline: A Memorial Day worth staying for.

milestone.label: What stood out
milestone.note: Professional races and the Memorial Day parachute demonstration

memory: I came back for BOLDERBoulder in 2023 because I had loved the experience the year before. I ran by myself again and was not chasing a particular time. I was there to enjoy the event.

After I finished, I stayed in Folsom Field to watch the professional races. That is one of the things that makes BOLDERBoulder feel so special: your own race leads into an afternoon of watching elite runners finish in the CU football stadium.

What I remember most from that year was the Memorial Day celebration in the stadium. There was a parachute demonstration with a member representing each service branch coming into Folsom Field. Staying after the race to watch that, along with the professionals, made the day feel like much more than a 10K.

colderbolder-2023.headline: The first leg of my Colorado Triathlon.
memory: I ran the COLDERBolder in 2023 mostly because it was a fun race, but that morning became the first leg of a much bigger day.

I had just bought my first mountain bike and wanted to take it out before winter really set in. Once I knew I was going to run and bike on the same day, I figured I might as well get a quick ski in too.

That turned the day into what I called the Colorado Triathlon: the COLDERBolder 5K, a quick ski at Eldora, then mountain biking at North Table Mountain. The race itself was just for fun, and it was a great way to start the day.

royal-gorge-groove-5k-2024.headline: A beautiful trail run to start the weekend.

milestone.label: Weekend
milestone.note: The first half of the Royal Gorge Groove weekend

memory: I remember driving out to Cañon City with Olive while it was pouring rain and checking into a terrible hotel. A new Taylor Swift album had just come out, and Olive and I listened to it like white noise so she would not bark every time somebody walked down the hallway.
The next day, the 5K itself was the complete opposite of the hotel experience. The trail course was beautiful, and I had a really good time running it.
It was also only the first half of the weekend. The plan was to come back the next day and race the mountain bike course on the same Royal Gorge trail system.

royal-gorge-groove-mtb-2024.headline: A race that showed me how much room I had to improve.

milestone.label: Challenge
milestone.note: A fun course and a real skills check

memory: The mountain bike race was much more challenging for me than the 5K had been the day before. I was still pretty new to mountain biking, and the course made that obvious in a good way.
I took my time on the descents, which meant I carried very little momentum into the climbs. I was cautious going downhill and then had to work hard to get back uphill again.

I really enjoyed the race, but I also finished it knowing how much room I had to improve. That is probably the biggest thing I remember from the ride: it was fun, it pushed me, and it gave me a very clear picture of the skills I still wanted to build.

colfax-5k-2024.headline: Running Colfax with Olive.

milestone.label: Together
milestone.note: A hot 5K with Leah and the dogs

memory: I ran the Colfax 5K with Olive, and Leah ran with Basil, Olive's sister. It was a hot day, but it was a really fun way to do the race together.
The heat is one of the things I remember most. At the finish they had little pools filled with ice water for the dogs, and Olive and Basil got to cool off right away.
That is what makes this 5K stand out in my memory: running it with Olive, sharing the day with Leah and Basil, and ending with the dogs cooling off together after the race.

photos.alt: Alex and Olive crossing the finish line at the 2024 Denver Colfax 5K.
photos.caption: Crossing the Colfax 5K finish with Olive.

photos.alt: Dogs cooling off in ice-water pools after the 2024 Denver Colfax 5K.
photos.caption: Olive and Basil cooling off in the ice-water pools after the hot 5K.

colfax-urban-10-2024.headline: My first run through Mile High Stadium.

milestone.label: First
milestone.note: A fun first run through the stadium

memory: The part of the 2024 Urban 10 Miler that stands out most is that it was my first time running through Mile High Stadium.
There was not some bigger meaning attached to it. It was just fun. Running through the stadium was a really cool part of the course and something I had never done before.
I had run the Colfax 5K the day before, so the 10 Miler completed a full Colfax weekend, but the stadium is the memory that separates this race for me.
